source.title: A Large Batch Optimizer Reality Check: Traditional, Generic Optimizers Suffice Across Batch Sizes
source.authors: Zachary Nado; J. Gilmer; Christopher J. Shallue; Rohan Anil; G. Dahl

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer choices and reports validation or downstream held-out performance, using different tasks and measures from the listed optimizer and batch-size claims. It does not directly measure the training–test generalization gap except for the ResNet-50 medians in Table 2.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own optimizer comparisons. The BERT F1 values are downstream SQuAD development-set results, not training-task generalization measurements. Results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: Table 4 tests V4 in a large-batch ImageNet setting: Adam and LAMB have lower validation accuracy than Nesterov momentum under restricted hyperparameter tuning. The study does not test V5 because it provides no own small-versus-large-batch comparison at a fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: standard Nesterov momentum and Adam match or exceed the large-batch results used to justify LARS and LAMB. The authors emphasize tuning effort, schedule shape, and pipeline details, and do not establish a universally superior optimizer.
record.recipe_differences: Compares large-batch optimizer configurations and validation/downstream performance rather than measuring generalization-gap predictors or the claim versions' interventions. It uses ImageNet ResNet-50 and BERT-Large; optimizer and hyperparameter tuning are central to the study.
record.method_sensitivity: The learning-rate schedule shape and optimizer interact; performance changes with step budget, epsilon, whether layerwise normalization is applied to bias and batch-normalization parameters, and hyperparameter tuning. The paper states that pure LAMB performs extremely poorly and that several configurations exceed the ImageNet target at 6,000 steps.

fits_no_version.finding: At 2,512 steps, Nesterov and LARS have similar validation accuracy, while Nesterov has higher training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise normalization of momentum can alter training fit without improving held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Independently tuned Adam exceeds cited LAMB downstream F1 at the matched 32k and hybrid batch regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise normalization is unnecessary for matching the reported large-batch BERT results.

fits_no_version.finding: At 6,000 steps, pure and hybrid LARS reach 76.9%, compared with Nesterov's 76.7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LARS and standard momentum can achieve similar large-batch ImageNet performance with a more generous training budget.

record.problems: The study says optimizer comparisons depend on independently and equally intensive tuning and does not claim either optimizer outperforms the other on the ResNet benchmark. BERT uses downstream SQuAD development-set F1 rather than a pretraining held-out metric; the authors note potential confounds. The 6,000-step ResNet comparison reports medians over 5 seeds of the best hyperparameter setting in a refined search space. The flattened Table 4 extraction leaves the pure-LAMB value-to-row assignment uncertain.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for cited prior results beyond the comparison values in Table 3. Tuning search trials, hyperparameter values, and ablation distributions are not extracted as claim outcomes. Appendix C figure-only ablation values are omitted because the plotted values are not stated numerically in the text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.

Equal or better adaptive-method training performance in the Table 4 comparison; whether broader tuning removes the adaptive-versus-SGD deficit; causal benefits of decoupling weight decay or switching to SGD; language-model comparisons against SGD. Table 4 tunes weight decay as well as learning rate, so it does not exactly reproduce the original learning-rate-and-schedule-only protocol.
Small-versus-large-batch held-out performance under matched epoch budgets, and whether recipe adaptations remove that measured penalty.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: A training–test gap measurement is unnecessary for V4's held-out-performance comparison. Conversely, exceeding an accuracy target at a large batch size alone does not establish V5's batch-size effect. Table 4 reports selected-setting medians, without uncertainty sufficient to establish statistical significance of the modest accuracy differences.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on the stated benchmarks; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay or switching to SGD, and word-level language models.
Comparison of large and small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that close the penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: Trained ImageNet classifier with Nesterov momentum Configuration B.

rows.note: No training-accuracy baseline for this subject; Table 2 reports the paired validation accuracy separately.

rows.note: The LAMB value is prior-work performance reproduced in the comparison table, not a run by this study.
rows.check: Adam versus cited LAMB performance does not test V4; differing batch regimes also do not supply a controlled V5 comparison.

rows.subject: Adam (with decoupled weight decay)
rows.stage_stated: pretraining, followed by fine-tuning on SQuAD v1.1
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained with Adam and evaluated after fine-tuning.
rows.note: No LAMB comparator is reported for this condition.
rows.check: Standalone downstream F1 lacks an SGD comparator or a controlled smaller-batch baseline.

rows.subject: Nesterov
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; Table 4 reports median top-1 validation accuracy over 5 seeds of the best hyperparameter setting.
rows.note: The paper compares optimizer configurations; no smaller-batch result is reported.
rows.check: Use as the momentum-SGD comparator for R11–R15: 76.7% validation accuracy. This is the median across five seeds at the selected hyperparameter setting.

rows.subject: LARS
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; LARS applied to weights and heavy-ball momentum to bias and batch-normalization parameters.
rows.note: The paper compares optimizer configurations; no smaller-batch result is reported.
rows.check: LARS versus Nesterov concerns layerwise normalization of momentum, rather than the Adam-like adaptive-method comparison in V4.

rows.subject: LARS
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; LARS applied to all parameters.
rows.note: The paper compares optimizer configurations; no smaller-batch result is reported.
rows.check: Pure LARS versus Nesterov concerns layerwise normalization of momentum; no batch-size comparison is provided.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; Adam applied to weights and bias/batch-normalization parameters, epsilon 10−8.
rows.note: The paper compares optimizer configurations; no smaller-batch result is reported.
rows.check: Supply R8 as baseline: Adam reaches 76.2% versus Nesterov's 76.7%. Learning rate and decoupled weight decay were tuned; most other Adam parameters were defaults.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; Adam applied to weights and bias/batch-normalization parameters, epsilon 10−6.
rows.note: The paper compares optimizer configurations; no smaller-batch result is reported.
rows.check: Supply R8 as baseline: Adam reaches 76.4% versus Nesterov's 76.7%, with epsilon fixed at 10^-6.

rows.subject: LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; LAMB applied to weights and bias/batch-normalization parameters.
rows.note: The paper states pure LAMB performs extremely poorly and only obtains reasonable results when not used on batch-normalization and bias parameters. The text extraction/table alignment makes assignment of 27.3 to this configuration unclear.
rows.check: The supplied Table 4 unambiguously assigns 27.3% to pure LAMB. Baseline is Nesterov's 76.7%. Appendix D.3 also reports frequent training divergence; this is principally an optimization failure.

rows.subject: LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; LAMB applied to weights, while Adam with epsilon 10−8 was applied to bias/batch-normalization parameters.
rows.note: The paper says LAMB obtains reasonable results when not applied to bias and batch-normalization parameters.
rows.check: Supply R8 as baseline: LAMB with Adam on bias/BN parameters reaches 76.3% versus Nesterov's 76.7%.

rows.subject: LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a cosine learning-rate schedule; LAMB applied to weights, while Adam with epsilon 10−6 was applied to bias/batch-normalization parameters.
rows.note: The paper says LAMB obtains reasonable results when not applied to bias and batch-normalization parameters.
rows.check: Supply R8 as baseline: LAMB with Adam on bias/BN parameters reaches 76.3% versus Nesterov's 76.7%.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50/ImageNet, batch 32,768, 6,000 steps, cosine schedule; Adam with learning rate and weight decay tuned
relationships.reason: R11–R12 reach 76.2–76.4% validation accuracy versus 76.7% for Nesterov in R8, even with decoupled weight decay.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam validation accuracy than Nesterov despite decoupled weight decay remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Same ImageNet budget; LAMB on weights and Adam on bias/BN parameters
relationships.reason: R14–R15 reach 76.3% versus Nesterov's 76.7% in R8 under the restricted tuning protocol.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower accuracy than Nesterov when combining LAMB with Adam remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Same ImageNet budget; pure LAMB applied to every parameter
relationships.reason: R13 reaches only 27.3% versus 76.7% in R8; frequent divergence identifies an optimization failure rather than an isolated generalization-gap effect.
relationships.display_finding: The reported severe accuracy deficit and frequent divergence with pure LAMB remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
